findings.title: Timed joins can leave old flusher processes running
findings.body: When `next_step.join(timeout)` consumes the timeout, `remaining_time <= 0` causes this loop to `break` before reaching the per-process `terminate()` call on line 346. The stopped flag is only observed after the worker finishes its current Redis/Kafka work, so these daemon workers can continue flushing while the consumer proceeds with rebalance/shutdown. A replacement strategy may then run workers for the same shards, causing concurrent duplicate production or continued resource use by a supposedly stopped consumer. Ensure all still-alive workers are terminated (and preferably joined) even when the join deadline has already elapsed.

findings.title: Non-positive flusher process counts are accepted without valid behavior
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` option accepts arbitrary integers. A negative value makes `num_processes` negative, produces an empty process map, and leaves the consumer writing spans to Redis with no flusher at all; Redis will eventually fill and halt ingestion. A value of zero is silently converted by `max_processes or len(...)` into one worker per shard, violating the documented maximum and potentially unexpectedly multiplying processes. Validate the CLI/configuration as at least 1 (for example with `click.IntRange(min=1)`) and avoid treating invalid values as defaults.
